name: Dorado PD Interceptor
_identity: TAUT AND FAST -- the reason a chase is a chase. The only profile in the fleet with a fully damped ride (6100 = 0.60 of critical) on short travel (0.34), the best tires (1.45), the stiffest lateral response (14500) and the strongest brakes (36000): it stays flat, it turns the instant you ask, and it stops. com_forward -0.06 puts 52.5% on the driven axle so it can actually use the 29000 N engine, which still exceeds rear grip -- stomp it and the back steps out, which is what makes cruisers ram and overshoot. top_speed 53 is one notch OVER the wrecker's 52 and six over the Brisket's 47: the truck out-drags it off the line (3.30 s to 20 m/s vs 4.00) and then loses the straight, every time.
_tuning_math: corner mass = 1820/4 = 455 kg; static load = 455*9.81 = 4463.6 N; spring_rate 56000 N/m -> static compression = 4463.6/56000 = 0.0797 m = 23.4% of suspension_rest 0.34 (stiff end of the 20-30% target); critical damping = 2*sqrt(56000*455) = 10096 N*s/m; damping 6100 = 0.604 * critical -- one bounce, no float, no wallow. Ride: pivot at -0.32-(0.34-0.0797) = -0.580, wheel radius 0.38 -> ground at -0.960 (0.035 m lower and 0.04 m less travel than the M10 setup: pursuit spec). com_height -0.46 puts the CoM 0.500 m above ground; static rollover threshold = half-track / CoM height = 0.90/0.500 = ~1.80 g against tire_friction 1.45 -- it will slide, hard, but it is the one car here that can never be flipped by its own tires. Rear-drive traction limit: rear axle carries (1.50+0.06)/3.05 = 51.1% of 1820 kg = 9128 N, x1.48 = 13509 N against 29000 N of engine -- launch is grip-limited with more than 2x the engine force in reserve, i.e. throttle-on oversteer is always one pedal away, and it still measures the shortest stop in the fleet (28.1 m from 30 m/s, tied with the wrecker and 13.8 m shorter than the Brisket) and by far the highest yaw rate (75.3 deg/s at full lock vs the Slab's 47.0).
